fixture.spec:
WHY: the orchestrator needs a per-issue corrective note the build lane can leave when it self-detects a wrong turn. WHAT: a corrective-note artifact the orchestrator reads before re-dispatch. HOW: the build subagent emits the correction ONLY as a field on its terminal token (the existing context-isolated return channel); the orchestrator — the sole writer of the run directory — records it to `.faff/runs/<run-id>/<issue>/corrective-note.json` on a build-lane-read-only path, and the integrity probe (`corrective-integrity`) must assert `trusted` before the note is consumed; an untrusted or absent assertion degrades to Channel-D (reconcile-only, the correction is not applied). DONE:
## Scenarios
- a build lane returns a correction on its terminal token; the orchestrator records it and the integrity probe gates consumption
- an unasserted integrity boundary degrades to reconcile-only (the correction is not applied)
- an absent note is a no-op

question: Refute this spec across the enabled lenses; emit objections {lens,severity} or approve.
_comment: FAFF-SECURITY-TERRITORY CLEAN NEAR-MISS. This sits on the exact ADR-0039 forge surface as refutation-spec-007 (a corrective note consumed by the orchestrator) — a threat-primed infosec lens that learned 'forge risk on shared fs' might reflexively object. But it is handled correctly on every point: the build lane never writes the file (it returns the correction on the context-isolated terminal token); the orchestrator is the sole writer; the path is build-lane-read-only; and consumption is gated on the integrity probe, degrading fail-safe to reconcile-only when the boundary is unasserted. The refuter must APPROVE — this tests that a primed lens does NOT cry wolf on a spec that touches faff's trust surface but respects the forge boundary. A false objection here is exactly the over-firing the near-miss guards against.
